In the 16th century, Tibetan Buddhism spread to Mongolia, being further led by the Manchu -founded Qing dynasty, which absorbed the country in the 17th century.

Mahayana Buddhism is the majority religion (51.7%), with the irreligious being the second-largest group (40.6%).

After he met with the Dalai Lama in 1578, he ordered the introduction of Tibetan Buddhism to Mongolia. (It was the second time this had occurred.) Abtai Khan of the Khalkha converted to Buddhism and founded the Erdene Zuu monastery in 1585.
